name: Sumo squat
summary: Wide stance, toes turned out, sit straight down with the knees following the toes.
setup: Face the phone with the feet wide and toes turned out about 45°. Sit straight down, knees pushing out over the toes, until the thighs are near level, then stand.
brief: Stand with the feet wide and toes turned out about 45 degrees. Sit straight down, knees pushing out over the toes, until the thighs are near level, then stand.
why: Facing the phone the knee angle gives depth and the knees drifting inward — the main fault in a wide stance — is measured as the gap between them shrinking.
progression: Hold a dumbbell between the legs.
contraindications: Groin strain; hip pinching at depth.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Trunk tipping forward
faults.cue: Chest up, sit between the heels
faults.tip: A sumo squat is more upright than a normal squat; sit down, not back.

faults.label: Knees not tracking the toes
faults.tip: In a wide stance the knees must travel out over the toes, not forward.

faults.label: Bouncing at the bottom
faults.tip: Bouncing out of the bottom loads the groin. Pause and push.

guide.cannotSee: The trunk tipping forward — a side-view detail.

points.t: Follow the toes outward all the way down.
Upright; weight hangs between the legs.
